note: Christmas Island is an external Territory of Australia, and the Privacy Act 1988 (Compilation No. 104, 4 June 2026), section 5A(1), says the Act extends to all external Territories (subsection (2) excepts only Schedule 2), so Australia's credit reporting rules in Part IIIA hold there, as they do in Australia (AU's file). The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner: a payment is missed if made more than 14 days after its due date, written as reported on the 15th day; repayment history stays on a credit report two years; the credit reporting bodies it names for a report are Equifax and Experian. A default (60 days, $150 and two notices) is a further listing, not modelled.

sources.title: Privacy Act 1988, Compilation No. 104 (4 June 2026), Federal Register of Legislation
sources.said: 5A Extension to external Territories (1) This Act extends to all external Territories. (2) This section does not apply to Schedule 2.

sources.title: OAIC, Repayment history and defaults
sources.said: This information remains on your credit report for 2 years. ... You are considered to have missed a payment if you make the payment more than 14 days after the due date.

sources.title: OAIC, Access your credit report
sources.said: You can request a copy of your credit report from these credit reporting bodies: Equifax , phone 138 332 Experian , phone 1300 783 684
